title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation scam in which AI-generated video was used to clone the likeness of a real, named attorney and deploy that likeness in fraudulent social media advertisements. The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI deployment. It occurred when actors used generative AI tools to produce convincing fake identity material and then ran those materials as paid or organic social media promotions targeting immigrants. The platform layer, where such ads are shown to users, is where detection would have needed to happen, through identity-verification checks on advertisers or automated flagging of synthetic media.

The scale detail in the summary, nearly 8,000 fake profile videos removed so far, indicates the fraudulent content was produced in volume and persisted long enough to reach victims across the country before removal. A victim had no institutional signal available to distinguish the fake from a legitimate attorney, because the ad used a real person's name and a realistic AI likeness. The additional pressure tactics, continuous document and payment requests followed by attempted extortion, are consistent with fraud operations that use an initial AI-generated hook and then shift to human operators.

It is not established who is responsible for creating or operating the scheme, and the single outlet report does not constitute a finding of criminal liability against any identified party.

reports.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A Bronx legal resident from the Dominican Republic lost $4,820 to an immigration scam using artificial intelligence. Victor Hernandez responded to a fake social media ad promising to help him become a U.S. citizen without taking the official exam for $1,500. Scammers continuously requested additional documents and money through the payment app Zelle, including his Social Security card and residency card. Hernandez only discovered the fraud after his wife suggested something seemed wrong and they consulted a friend. The fake advertisement used AI technology combined with the stolen identity of real immigration attorney Angel Leal from Miami, who had no involvement in the scheme.

Leal reports that his identity has been cloned to create multiple fraudulent profiles, with nearly 8,000 fake profile videos removed so far. Scammers have used his AI-generated likeness to victimize immigrants across the country. After discovering the scam, the criminals attempted to extort additional money from Hernandez. Now behind on rent and electricity bills, Hernandez filed reports with NYPD and federal law enforcement and worries about identity theft consequences. Attorney Leal advises people not to hire lawyers through social media, to meet attorneys in person, and to avoid anyone requesting payment through cash-sending apps.
